steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Classical Hollywood narrative is the dominant storytelling model in US cinema, characterised by cause-and-effect logic, goal-oriented protagonists, narrative closure and invisible filmmaking style.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The three-act structure divides the narrative into setup (establishing characters and conflict), confrontation (complications and obstacles) and resolution (climax and closure).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cause-and-effect logic means that events in the narrative are driven by character decisions and actions rather than coincidence, creating a sense of narrative necessity and coherence.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The protagonist in classical Hollywood is typically an active, goal-driven individual whose desires define the narrative trajectory and whose actions propel the plot forward.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Apply narrative theory specifically to your set film — do not discuss theory in the abstract without concrete examples. Identify where your film follows and where it deviates from classical Hollywood conventions — most films do both. Use precise theoretical terminology: 'enigma code', 'binary opposition', 'new equilibrium' rather than vague descriptions. Explain how narrative structure creates meaning, not just how it organises events — structure itself is ideological. When discussing alternative narratives, explain what the deviation from classical norms achieves rather than simply noting that it is different.
